XMLDB.COMMENT: Sentientia LMS Calendar Sync — Phase 1 (outbound ICS feed token storage) + Phase 2 (OAuth scaffolding for Microsoft 365 + Google Calendar). The Phase 2 table is additive; the Phase 1 table is unchanged.

TABLE.NAME: local_sentientia_calendar_token
TABLE.COMMENT:
Tier 2.6 Phase 1 (2026-05-24) — One row per user per active ICS subscription token. The token is a 64-character random string embedded in the subscription URL the user pastes into Outlook / Google / Apple Calendar. The token is the authentication mechanism — calendar clients fetch the feed without browser cookies, so cookie-based session auth is not available.
A user may have at most one ACTIVE (revoked=0) token at a time; regenerate revokes the old one and creates a new one. Revoked rows are kept for audit (we can answer 'who used a leaked token, when?'). Periodic cleanup deletes revoked rows older than 90 days via the purge_old_tokens scheduled task.
Multi-customer scope: each row carries customerid + tenantid so future per-customer reporting can answer 'how many users in Customer N have subscribed?'.
GDPR / privacy: the token alone does not identify the user to an outside party. last_used_at + last_used_ip are useful for abuse forensics; both purge with the row after 90-day retention.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: FK to mdl_user.id — the user whose calendar this token unlocks

FIELD.NAME: customerid
FIELD.COMMENT: Sentientia LMS customer scope. Phase 1: hardcoded 1 (Airpay) per customer::current().

FIELD.NAME: tenantid
FIELD.COMMENT: BizLMS tenant root (1=Airpay, 77=Public, 177=ZEEA). Derived from user open_path at insert time.

FIELD.NAME: token
FIELD.COMMENT: 64-char URL-safe random token (alphanumeric). Used as the URL query parameter that authenticates the request.

FIELD.NAME: revoked
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 = active, 1 = revoked (user regenerated). Revoked tokens never authenticate again.

FIELD.NAME: last_used_at
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix ts of last successful feed fetch (NULL = never used)

FIELD.NAME: last_used_ip
FIELD.COMMENT: IPv4 / IPv6 of the last fetch. Diagnostic only.

FIELD.NAME: use_count
FIELD.COMMENT: Total successful fetch count. Helps identify abandoned subscriptions.

KEY.NAME: uk_token
KEY.COMMENT: Token alone authenticates — must be globally unique

INDEX.NAME: idx_user_revoked
INDEX.COMMENT: Lookup current active token for a user

INDEX.NAME: idx_timemodified
INDEX.COMMENT: Purge query for revoked rows older than retention window

TABLE.NAME: local_sentientia_calendar_oauth
TABLE.COMMENT:
Tier 2.6 Phase 2 (2026-05-24) — Encrypted-at-rest OAuth 2.0 token storage for Microsoft 365 (Microsoft Graph) and Google Calendar. One row per (user, provider) pair — a user may have one m365 row AND one google row at the same time, but not two m365 rows.
access_token_enc and refresh_token_enc are emitted by \core\encryption::encrypt() (Sodium AES-via-secretbox under the hood). Plaintext tokens NEVER appear in the column. Recovering a token requires both this DB row AND $CFG->dataroot/secret/key/sodium.key (chmod 0400 by Moodle). The encryption is reversible only on the same Moodle instance that created it — moving a DB dump to a different Moodle (without copying the key file) leaves the tokens unrecoverable.
expires is the unix timestamp at which the access_token expires. Callers compare against time() to decide whether to call the refresh flow before using the access_token.
scopes is the space-separated scope string the provider granted at consent time. Comparing this against the scopes you NEED at call time lets you detect downgrade (the user denied a scope on a re-consent) and re-prompt before failing the API call.
GDPR / DPDP: every column on this row is PII (a refresh_token implicitly authenticates the user to the provider for months). Privacy provider exports METADATA only (provider name, expires, scopes, timestamps) — the encrypted tokens themselves are never written into the user's export archive.
SCAFFOLDING note (Phase 2): the surfaces that would populate this table — oauth_connect.php + oauth_callback.php — are NOT shipped in this chip. The schema is in place; Phase 2.1 wires up the live HTTP exchange that produces real rows here.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: FK to mdl_user.id — the user whose calendar this token authorises us to touch

FIELD.NAME: customerid
FIELD.COMMENT: Sentientia LMS customer scope. Phase 1: hardcoded 1 (Airpay) per customer::current().

FIELD.NAME: provider
FIELD.COMMENT: Provider identifier — currently 'm365' (Microsoft Graph) or 'google' (Google Calendar). Matches oauth_base subclass PROVIDER constant.

FIELD.NAME: access_token_enc
FIELD.COMMENT: Encrypted (Sodium secretbox via \\core\\encryption::encrypt) access_token. Typical plaintext is ~1-2 KB JWT; encrypted ciphertext is base64 + IV + tag overhead.

FIELD.NAME: refresh_token_enc
FIELD.COMMENT: Encrypted refresh_token. NULL or empty-string-encrypted when the provider didn't mint one (e.g. Google without prompt=consent). Long-lived (months); the high-value secret.

FIELD.NAME: expires
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix ts when the access_token expires. 0 = unknown / not set.

FIELD.NAME: scopes
FIELD.COMMENT: Space-separated scope string the provider GRANTED at consent (may differ from what we requested).

KEY.NAME: uk_user_provider
KEY.COMMENT: One row per (user, provider). Re-connecting UPDATEs the existing row in place.

INDEX.NAME: idx_provider_expires
INDEX.COMMENT: Background refresh job query — find tokens expiring soon, per provider

INDEX.NAME: idx_customer_provider
INDEX.COMMENT: Per-customer subscription stats (e.g. 'how many m365 connections in customer 1?')
